result.summary: The intersection is equipped with high-visibility continental crosswalks and basic sidewalk infrastructure in a residential neighborhood. However, the lack of dedicated pedestrian signals and physical traffic calming measures like curb extensions increases the risk for people crossing the street.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible, requiring pedestrians to rely on vehicle traffic lights which may not provide adequate clearance time.

hazards.name: Wide turning radius
hazards.description: The absence of curb extensions allows vehicles to make right turns at higher speeds, increasing the risk of conflict with pedestrians in the crosswalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Corner of the intersection near the utility pole

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signals with countdown timers to provide clear information on remaining crossing time.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signal to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle traffic gets a green light.

result.summary: The image depicts a signalized intersection with high-visibility continental crosswalk markings and continuous sidewalks. result.summary: The intersection is equipped with marked zebra crosswalks, pedestrian signals, and sidewalks on both sides. While basic infrastructure is present, the wide roadway and lack of physical traffic calming measures may allow for higher vehicle speeds and longer exposure for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Wide Turning Radius
hazards.description: The corner geometry on the right allows vehicles to make right turns at relatively high speeds, increasing risk to pedestrians in the crosswalk.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical buffer or planting strip between the sidewalk and the roadway, placing pedestrians in close proximity to moving traffic.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and tighten the turning radius for vehicles, slowing down turning traffic.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signal to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle traffic gets a green light.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a wide, two-lane roadway with a sidewalk on one side but no marked crossing facilities across the main thoroughfare. The lack of traffic control or pedestrian-specific infrastructure creates a high-exposure environment for those attempting to cross.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: There is no marked crosswalk across the main thoroughfare at this intersection, forcing pedestrians to cross without designated space.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb obstruct the view between pedestrians waiting to cross and oncoming drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the roadway along the curb
